scope: Original cold-boot camera entry versus already-running camera normal-stop maintenance. Catalog only; no executor or code change.

coordination_interface.effect: Do not infer a fresh cold-boot state, board ownership handoff, current boot/marker/head, or execution authorization from this source catalog. Main/cold branch must read and pin the actual interface when supplied. Device calls remain frozen.

decision_cases.case: Current boot camera has never committed its counter domain
requires_fresh_proof: Actual current boot and no live/uncertain camera Native/VART/DPU/MMIO owner; no pending service job
A real pinned sealed predecessor checkpoint belongs to a different boot; original source closure and original config opt-ins remain valid
The configured current-kernel marker path does not exist, including no partial file or symlink; MainPID0 alone does not prove this
Actual original service entry/drop-ins/meta/settings/library/C-unit provenance and original platform requirements match; no historical owner/head is inserted
decision_cases.original_path: native_startup.preflight selects native_boot.load_new_boot_checkpoint; original attach later calls commit_new_boot once before NativeContext restore/adopt
decision_cases.old_checkpoint_consumed_marker: The prior checkpoint-specific consumed marker may already exist from its prior boot. The different-boot loader intentionally checks the current-kernel marker instead; preserve both marker families and use the original cross-boot archive-only path.
decision_cases.not_applicable: Do not invent a current-owner stop-intent or feed this branch to load_business_checkpoint/current-final normal-stop validator.

decision_cases.case: Camera is already running and needs a maintenance source update
requires_fresh_proof: Actual boot/PID/birth/cmd and original running config/source pins
Original GUI normal stop, idle listening/enrollment/playback, exclusive maintenance handoff and effective infinite no-SIGKILL camera stop protection
One real original normal camera stop, durable intent and fresh same-boot final whose source owner/time/counters match this attempt
Original current-final reader and complete expected history/current bounds verification; unconsumed fresh final before normal restart
decision_cases.original_path: native_startup.preflight selects load_business_checkpoint; attach restores exact same-boot seed then consume_checkpoint; shutdown writes the next real final
decision_cases.history_scope: Same-boot restart carries the existing previous_kernel_history link; it does not create a new boot archive/counter domain.
decision_cases.not_applicable: Do not bypass a consumed same-boot final by directly calling the different-boot loader or changing a boot ID.

decision_cases.case: No camera PID is present but the current-kernel domain marker already exists
decision_cases.required_handling: This is not proved to be an unstarted cold boot. An earlier attach may have committed the marker and then failed. Original loader refuses a second new domain; retain evidence and follow the original lifecycle/uncertain-result handling. A valid unconsumed current-boot final, if actually present, is a separate same-boot resume case.
decision_cases.forbidden_shortcuts: No marker removal, zero seed, changed boot field, fabricated stop-intent, guessed final, repeated start, or replay of a historical checkpoint to obtain another budget.

original_apis.input: Original complete native_execution keys: library/library_sha256, seed pin, source_manifest/source_manifest_sha256, source_unit_sha256, checkpoint_output. Optional explicit allow_new_kernel_boot, allow_legacy_new_kernel_boot and new_boot_marker_directory.
original_apis.output: Validated native dict or None; exact Python rglob('*.py') manifest closure required.
original_apis.checks: Original detector dpu_yolox, conservative admission floor30ms, both recovery policies and0..100ms waits remain enforced. The legacy opt-in additionally requires the new-boot opt-in.
original_apis.side_effects: Read/validate metadata and code hashes. configuration marker_paths validation does not create a directory or consume a domain.
original_apis.reuse: Original support functions, not a cold-start executor. Python backups must remain outside the AURA rglob source tree.

original_apis.input: Actual boot_id, actual AURA root, original config and real pinned predecessor.
original_apis.output: loaded object from same-boot load_business_checkpoint OR different-boot load_new_boot_checkpoint; predecessor document source_unit must match the configured provenance.
original_apis.routing: Read source boot from sealed seed.boot_id or explicit legacy source_boot. Same boot always selects business reader; different boot requires allow_new_kernel_boot and original configured marker directory. It is not selected by whether a camera PID is visible.
original_apis.side_effects: Original function validates/read-only loads metadata, checks Python/tracker source closure and actual boot. No commit, marker write, NativeContext instance or model inference in this function. Installed identity_recovery can wrap it and add audit/config mutation, so the runtime ns.preflight name is not necessarily the bare original.
original_apis.reuse: Original loader contract is reusable in the normal entry. A separate isolated metadata call would need its original dependency/import audit and fresh owner exclusion; no call is made by this catalog.

original_apis.input: Original sealed-v2 document or explicitly supported legacy health-prefix document, each in its own archived boot.
original_apis.output: Validated archive seed/auxiliary. Legacy returns lower-bound/unknown-tail archive-only state and never an exact resumable C seed.
original_apis.side_effects: Pure original semantic validation and ctypes Seed/Recovery structure construction for v2; no NativeContext/CDLL/restore or state write. Old captured/recovery times are evaluated only against their archived capture.
original_apis.reuse: Directly reusable pure definitions for a correctly pinned archive-only audit. They do not by themselves prove full linked-history completeness or authorize startup.

original_apis.input: Real different-boot predecessor pin, actual current boot, actual configured marker directory and explicit legacy boolean.
original_apis.output: loaded.new_kernel_boot=True; a new RAM seed purpose validated_new_kernel_boot, source_pid/birth0, current-boot monotonic capture and clean zero current counters; archive_seed/archive_auxiliary/archive_counters retain the complete predecessor domain separately. Document/SHA/source_path and current-kernel marker identity remain attached.
original_apis.checks: checked_boot actual match; original _sealed_source or separately opted-in _legacy_source; source boot must differ; current-kernel marker lexists must be false. It deliberately does not reject merely because the old checkpoint-specific consumption marker exists.
original_apis.side_effects: Read-only metadata checks plus a fresh in-memory seed and time sample. No marker/archive write, NativeContext, restore, model or device operation. It does not recursively audit all older archive links.
original_apis.reuse: Original different-boot loader can be reused under its real cold-entry contract; never force a same-boot predecessor through it or treat its RAM seed as a manually written checkpoint.

original_apis.input: Untampered loaded object from original different-boot loader; actual boot, source pin, archive seed and exact fresh seed are revalidated.
original_apis.output: Mutates loaded by adding archive_path/archive_sha256; persists original previous-kernel archive and current-kernel consumption record.
original_apis.side_effects: Creates/verifies effective-UID-owned0700 marker/archive directories. Writes/fsyncs a unique temporary archive and hard-links exact bytes to archive/<actualboot>-<actual predecessor SHA>.json. Then O_EXCL creates/fsyncs kernel-boot-<actualboot>.consumed. Existing identical archive is accepted; any existing marker prevents a new domain. A partial/failed marker is deliberately retained. No original checkpoint overwrite or old marker removal.
original_apis.reuse: Effectful one-time commit, NOT a reader or dry-run. Must remain in original attach ordering. Do not call it just to test cold readiness or retry after an uncertain commit.

original_apis.input: Validated loaded plus original YOLO owner whose fixed-input checks already passed, runtime state and original configured library.
original_apis.output: NativeYoloOwner and NativeDpuSchedule, with exact same-boot handoff OR native_new_kernel_boot metadata and archived previous_kernel_history link.
original_apis.side_effects: Cold branch commits archive/current-kernel marker BEFORE creating NativeContext and restoring/adopting. Same-boot branch restores exact sealed seed then calls consume_checkpoint before adopt. Constructs/loads Native library, adopts original model owner and enables the existing business scheduler. Errors retain unconfirmed native ownership; they do not restore a fresh budget.
original_apis.reuse: Production lifecycle step only, not directly callable as offline readiness or metadata validation. A commit followed by context failure still consumes the cold domain.

original_apis.input: Current real owner only after camera/identity workers have joined and their runners closed, complete SFace seven-counter state and optional histories.
original_apis.output: Original new final pin from native context checkpoint and write_checkpoint; carries the existing hash-linked previous_kernel_history.
original_apis.side_effects: Actual Native checkpoint operation, original final JSON write and owner close. Writes the current running manifest SHA, not an assumed prior manifest. No new boot archive is made on a same-boot stop.
original_apis.reuse: Only by the real normal shutdown lifecycle. Cannot synthesize this outcome for a boot where camera has not run.

known_entry_chain_reference.outer_and_feed: Pinned face ingress validates its deployment manifest and installs original face/raw timing hooks. Operator entry validates op7 runtime-manifest/settings and installs the existing recovery wrapper. Feed entry validates APP_PINS/meta/protected native_entry and redirects only the original camera runpy target to camera_wrapper. Bypassing the top entry drops these existing integration hooks.
known_entry_chain_reference.original_native_entry_input: OPS/meta.json and candidate_config. It selects the existing checkpoint_output bytes and computes their real SHA when present; it does not hardcode a seed SHA. Original meta.source_boot remains a protection-domain condition and is not rewritten to the current boot.
known_entry_chain_reference.original_native_entry_side_effects: Creates native-run-<actualboot>-<actualpid>/config.json, adjusts argv/sys.path/switch interval and runs original camera. If native_binding._RETAINED is nonempty, writes UNSAFE_OWNER_RETAINED.json and holds the process on SIGTERM/SIGINT rather than replacing an uncertain owner.
known_entry_chain_reference.camera_run_order: ui_camera_service.run resolves camera, calls native preflight, then checked_backend loads original models and runs real fixed-reference/blank inference checks, then attach, then existing lock/workers/preview. Its finally joins workers/closes identity before shutdown. Normal service startup is therefore real device/model work, not a preflight-only probe.
known_entry_chain_reference.identity_recovery_side_effects: Installed preflight enforces explicit predecessor-library and allowed ABI-compatible unit migration, substitutes the runtime operator library/unit around original preflight and writes recovery-audit JSON. NativeContext optional calls get existing scoped realtime scheduling. SFace initialization starts a recovery worker; when its stored request_boot differs from actual boot, that worker returns before its operator marker/request path. When they match it can create an operator marker, request native recovery and run bounded synthetic SFace health probes. Do not update old request_boot/settings to re-arm this behavior as a cold-start repair.
known_entry_chain_reference.classification: These are original implementation sources, not historical action recipes. The operational entry is the actual currently installed normal service entry after fresh closure verification; do not directly run a cached Python entry or import camera_wrapper merely to inspect it.

boot_ops_interface.inputs: Actual OPS root/meta/state/source pins/protected files plus current kernel. gate delegates to policy.condition(meta.source_boot, actualboot, phase, role).
boot_ops_interface.pure_policy_output: Boolean role/phase admission; it does not validate or consume a seed or establish a counter domain. Camera and GUI phase admission differ.
boot_ops_interface.read_only_subcommands: condition returns gate exit status; status reads state and any referenced benchmark JSON. Neither substitutes for full source/owner/marker/cold-loader checks.
boot_ops_interface.effectful_actions: Controller methods can change maintenance phases/drop-ins/timers, stop/start/reset services, reboot, run real model benchmarks, restore a different legacy entry, or configure rollback. activate writes the original Restart=no/KillMode=process/TimeoutStopSec=infinity/SendSIGKILL=no execution drop-in and starts camera; this is a specific old maintenance state transition, not a universal cold-start command.
boot_ops_interface.reuse_boundary: Preserve current original ExecCondition/state machine and no-kill protections. Read/diagnose a gate failure under a future handoff; do not forge phase/meta, call benchmark/activate/rescue to manufacture eligibility, or replay its original maintenance workflow.

maintenance_only_templates.role: Fresh already-running owner maintenance normal-stop candidate; its dry-run requires active camera and captured current health/bounds. It is inapplicable to a cold boot with no camera owner, and no stop-intent should be manufactured.

Offline-reviewed same-boot current-final + complete-history maintenance validator. Requires real current-owner normal-stop intent/result, same-boot fresh final and independently sourced history. Not a cold pre-camera entry, not a cross-boot loader.
Original load_business_checkpoint read-only recipe only. A previous-boot/already-consumed predecessor fails its same-boot/marker contract; do not relax it for cold startup.

Historical archive-only recipe contains fixed former head/count/context. Its original pure archived validation is a reference; the cached top-level invocation is not directly reusable with a fresh boot.
Historical fixed-owner stop action template; not an executable fresh cold/maintenance contract.

fresh_inputs_left_required: Actual published BOOT_RECOVERY_INTERFACE.json and its SHA/ownership freeze instructions
Actual boot, service/cgroup/jobs, old/current owner identities and current-kernel marker existence; distinguish never-started from failed-after-commit
Actual current entry/drop-ins/meta/state/settings/source closures/library/C-unit and configured new-boot marker directory
Actual prior sealed checkpoint pin and source boot; preserve existing checkpoint-specific/current-kernel markers
Full original archive-only semantic/provenance chain with real head/count/legacy scope; do not substitute the maintenance stop validator

Normal camera start only after the owning branch's fresh authorization and platform/source/owner prerequisites; then original archive/marker audit, real run config/owner and selected GUI source rebinding
